title: Expectation under product selector sampling
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n\geq 0$, and let $\theta\in[-1,1]$. Independently sample two vectors $U,V\in\Omega^n$ by drawing each coordinate from $\pi$. Also sample a pair of sign vectors $(R,T)\in\{-1,1\}^n\times\{-1,1\}^n$ from the correlated sign-pair distribution with parameter $\theta$. Form vectors $X,Y\in\Omega^n$ coordinatewise by setting $X_i=U_i$ when $R_i=1$ and $X_i=V_i$ otherwise, and setting $Y_i=U_i$ when $T_i=1$ and $Y_i=V_i$ otherwise. For every $H:\Omega^n\times\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, its expectation at the pair $(X,Y)$ equals the nested expectation obtained by first averaging over $U$, then over $V$, and then over $(R,T)$.
hypotheses_covered: A probability mass function on the sample set
A real-valued function on pairs of coordinate vectors
